item.content:encoded:
I would concur with FFB's assessment as well. Funny, yes, but mean-spirited. The site essentially belonged to these members we now ridicule for their OTT co-opting of the narrative. Personally, I hated it and felt bullied out of contributing, but comic vengeance doesn't really produce anything new or worthwhile, however satisfying or amusing it may be. The site was here for our latter-day caretakers to re-invent because of these folks, as much as we might mislike their hijinks.

Time has changed the tone of the site, but the day may come when our current standard-enforcers are the ones being ridiculed.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm going to abstain from voting, but I will voice my opinion that derivative parody works of OTT Senior Staff hijinks do not add significant value to the body of work that the SCP Foundation has come to represent for me. Maybe I'm taking things too seriously today, but while this is fun, it amounts basically to a public shaming of a reasonably popular story.

I find it a bit mean-spirited and unoriginal, and it's troubling that this isn't the first time I've seen an article like this with a strong positive rating while other tales, genuine efforts at creating original content, have been discredited and deleted for being insufficiently groundbreaking.

That's what I have to say. An unpopular opinion perhaps, but I felt I needed to share it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: And no better for it, since the original is so bad it reads as self-parody anyways. This makes an attempt to go for laughs by amplifying the slapdash weirdness of its model to absurdity, but the problem there is that this is stupid, because something as gibberingly moronic as the original is already absurd. So this doesn't read as a criticism. It reads as an unfunny redundancy.
